pr_title: fix(localize): support inlined downleveled  es5 localize call
pr_body:
When the downleveling helper function has been  inlined into the
`$localize` call, it is a bit more tricky to parse out the cooked and
raw strings. There was already code to do this but it assumed that
the `cooked` and `raw` items were both arrays.

Sometimes the `raw` array is just a copy of the `cooked` array
via an expression similar to `raw || (raw=tcookedslice(0))`. This
commit changes the `unwrapMessagePartsFromLocalizeCall()`
function to be able to handle such a situation.

Fixes #40702

issue_context.title: localize doesn't work with target: ES2015
issue_context.body:
I'm working with angular since several years now and localization is a problem again and again.
First it starts with the question, how should the ecosystem around translation look like, what's the best practice here? There is no documentation, recommendation or help for the steps after extracting i18n.
It start's with the fact, that translations by default are not merged, so I added xliffmerge do my stack. That works pretty okay.
For doing translations I use [poedit](https://poedit.net) which is also a pretty nice tool.

But in the end I regularly get issues broken translations, because interpolation doesn't correctly find it self through the process or currently with this _Unexpected messageParts for `$localize` (expected an array of strings)._. This error message itself is already a pain because it's not helpful at all, because it actually just tells you "There is something wrong with your translations, good luck finding the bad one".

The problem for me is, that I really don't know who to "blame". Is angular not creating proper XLIFF files, is xliffmerge not merging them correctly or is poedit doing something wrong with my files. It's really frustrating to work with translations when beeing confronted with such errors.

So I really hope that the angular team can spend some time to add documentation about tools that are proven to work with angular. To think about integrating xliffmerge into angular CLI and to add more helpful error messages so that broken translations can be identified easier.

P.S.: Oh and what I forgot is prettier. It also adds to the mess because messages are wrapped or spaces are added which makes creating translations also harder.

I reverse engineered that AST and it looks something like this:

```js
e || (t=[""], n || (n=t.slice(0)), e = Object.freeze(Object.defineProperties(t, {raw: {value: Object.freeze(n)}}))
```

So the overall `$localize` call will be:

```js
var e,t,n;
$localize(e ||
  (
    t=[""],
    n || (n=t.slice(0)),
    e = Object.freeze(Object.defineProperties(t, {raw: {value: Object.freeze(n)}}))
  )
)
```

This is basically a downleveling of 

```
$localize``
```

In other words some aspect of your build system is converting the tagged template literal and generating a call.
Different transpilers can generate different version of this. We have the ability to parse various forms of this.
See https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bb6d791dab5c74ae7571cd68ee7cddf322247dc6/packages/localize/src/tools/test/source_file_utils_spec.ts#L79-L166

It seems that this is another format that we have not come across before. It would necessary to know more about the build tooling you are using to generate these files.

This thread is tracking 2 issues it seems.

1) Better error messages for i18n
2) A regression in angular 11.1.2 that caused errors on previously working repos.

I see 1) is being addressed, but what about 2) ?

Thanks for the clarification :)
The second one is also being addressed. See https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/40702#issuecomment-773634754

Interestingly Babel generates code that we can already handle. I have added extra tests for the new cases that were added in https://github.com/babel/babel/pull/12588.

What I think has actually happened in this case is that the helper that Babel uses has been inlined by some other tool (perhaps terser?).

Babel would produce something like:
```js
$localize(e || (n || (n=babelHelpers.taggedTemplateLiteral(''))))
```

But this code is
```js
$localize(e || (t=[""], n || (n=t.slice(0)), e = Object.freeze(Object.defineProperties(t, {raw: {value: Object.freeze(n)}})))
```

So we need to grab the array that `t` has been initialized to...
